title: Healthy Hamburger Helper
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.notes: 93/7 lean grind, not 80/20. The source states 'lean', a real price class apart from 80/20, so the 'ground beef' -> ground-beef-8020 precedent for an UNQUALIFIED line does not transfer; the vocabulary's own 93/7 Ground Beef row is the lean grind. Protein confirms it: 41.8 g/serving against the source's published 40, where 80/20 gives 37.0 and fails the floor.

'Finely chopped' is a prep word, not a food; unqualified cooking onion is the yellow onion per the 'med onion' and 'small yellow onion' precedents, and red is refused on variety pricing. Board 7 of 7; half a cup chopped weighs 80 g.

macro_cross_check: Source published 507 cal / 40 protein for 4 servings. Recomputed over all 14 lines at source basis: 2315 cal and 167 g protein total, i.e. 579 cal and 41.8 g protein per serving. Protein is +4.5% against the source, well inside 15%, which is the check that matters and it lands on the main protein. Calories run +14%, mostly the dry-pasta basis and full-fat cheddar. Same arithmetic with 80/20 beef gives 37.0 g protein per serving, below this run's 40 g floor, which is the concrete reason the lean grind was ruled and not bridged.
